name: Roomote Docs
description: Documentation for Roomote, the open, self-hostable platform for cloud coding agents.

instructions: When helping someone deploy Roomote, distinguish self-hosting from contributing to Roomote. Use the Self-hosting guide for an operator deployment; use Local development only when the user intends to modify Roomote itself.

When an agent is asked to follow /self-hosting or install Roomote autonomously, read and follow /self-hosting/agent-installation as the normative automation contract even though it is intentionally hidden from side navigation.
Prefer the one-command installer on a fresh supported server unless the user explicitly chooses Roomote Cloud, a documented PaaS template, or a manual Compose deployment.

Detect the host and choose documented defaults before asking questions: install directly on a supported Ubuntu/Debian Linux server or VPS; for local macOS or Windows evaluation, create or reuse a full Ubuntu Linux VM and run Docker and Roomote inside it; do not overclaim WSL2 support or treat Docker Desktop as the Linux installer host.

For a local evaluation that needs OAuth or webhook reachability and has no supplied stable public domain, default to cloudflared inside the Linux guest and a temporary HTTPS Quick Tunnel, configure Roomote from the generated trycloudflare.com hostname, and explain that tunnel restarts require installer metadata and provider callback updates and that wildcard previews are unavailable. For durable VPS or production installs, default to stable DNS, public HTTPS, Caddy, and ports 80/443; use a named tunnel only when stable closed-port ingress is required.

Proceed with safe, reversible documented defaults when access is already available. Ask only when privileges are unavailable, credentials or browser authorization are needed, durable external state such as DNS/firewalls/account resources must change, an operation is destructive or skips backup, existing deployment state conflicts, or no safe default exists. Batch related approvals after reporting the exact planned actions.

Never ask the user to paste secrets into chat or commit real environment files. Put credentials in the deployment platform's secret manager, Roomote's setup UI, or protected environment variables, and preserve existing keys during upgrades and restores.

Prefer Roomote's setup wizard and provider manifest flows over manual credential entry when those flows are available. Pause for user credentials or browser authorization and ask before durable external-account or destructive changes; do not ask merely because a documented reversible default uses privileges the agent already has.

A setup is not complete when the services merely start. Verify sign-in, repository sync, one usable environment, a real task that can clone and run a command, and branch or pull-request delivery; verify previews when configured.

For a persistent self-hosted deployment, leave the operator with the Roomote URL, deployment choices, configured providers, verification result, backup location and passphrase-handling reminder, and the roomote status, logs, upgrade, rollback, backup, and restore commands.
